subject: EdgeFuse demarcation & uplink topology review (control-relay / data-striping)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: EdgeFuse Ops <ops@edgefuse.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeFuse demarcation & uplink topology review (control-relay / data-striping)

Hi team — attaching the first-pass reference diagrams for the EdgeFuse private deployment we discussed during last week's runbook sync. The two areas we want to validate with your network team are: 1) control-plane relay placement (where callbacks/health-checks terminate inside the customer VPC) and 2) data-plane uplink striping for inference traffic to satisfy the SLA without breaking tenant isolation.

Attachments: edgefuse_vpc_v1.pdf, egress_matrix.csv, redwood_controlplane_mapping.xlsx

High level requests: 
- Can EdgeFuse confirm a recommended NAT+BGP demarc option versus a public egress proxy? We prefer BGP demarc for predictable latency but want to confirm ops cost.
- Validate the control-plane relay design in diagram A: single relay per AZ vs region-level relay. Tradeoffs are listed on slide 3.
- Confirm whether we can rely on an existing VPC S2S peering or if a dedicated transit is required for telemetry (Prometheus traces, KV cache prefetch).

Please review and call out any non-starter items by EOD Wed (20 Jun). If you want a short 30-min walkthrough, we can schedule tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: EdgeFuse Ops <ops@edgefuse.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFuse demarcation & uplink topology review (control-relay / data-striping)

Thanks Neha — these look good as a starting point. A few quick clarifying Qs from NetEng: 

1) NAT vs BGP demarc: we can support both, but for your listed latency target (p99 < 60ms) we recommend BGP with ECMP and a small pool of egress accelerators. NAT adds unpredictable SNAT state churn on bursts.

2) Control-plane relay: region-level relay is our operational preference (one relay per region, active/passive with health-probes). Single relay per AZ increases operational overhead and cross-AZ data charges for your telemetry. Can you confirm whether telemetry can be replicated over our secure peering?

3) Telemetry channels: we need an allowlist of IPs and an ingress CIDR for the relay. Also confirm if mutual mTLS termination is required at the relay (we support mTLS + client cert pinning).

We reviewed the egress_matrix.csv — one suggested change: for tenant-critical flows mark 10.0.48.0/22 as "no-cache" because the KV cache sits on the customer side for that workload. See inline comments.

Would like that 30-min walkthrough to validate assumptions. Are you available Wed 20 Jun 11:00-11:30 PDT?

Regards,
Maya Singh (on behalf of EdgeFuse NetEng)
EdgeFuse Operations
ops@edgefuse.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFuse demarcation & uplink topology review (control-relay / data-striping)

On Tue, 19 Jun 2028 at 10:15 AM EdgeFuse Ops <ops@edgefuse.com> wrote:
> Thanks Neha — these look good as a starting point. A few quick clarifying Qs from NetEng: 
> 
> 1) NAT vs BGP demarc: we can support both, but for your listed latency target (p99 < 60ms) we recommend BGP with ECMP and a small pool of egress accelerators. NAT adds unpredictable SNAT state churn on bursts.

Thanks — agree with the BGP recommendation. A few technical constraints from our runtime team: 
- The control-plane relay must maintain sticky TCP sessions for KV cache warmups and long-poll health checks. If you do region-level relay, ensure session affinity across ECMP or we will see cache-warm misses that spike tail latency.
- For telemetry we will only send non-sensitive traces over the peering; sensitive audit logs must go to the customer's logging collector over a separate TLS stream (see diagram B, note 2).
- mTLS is required end-to-end for control-plane API calls (Redwood policy). EdgeFuse can terminate mTLS at the relay only if you provide a signed CSR per region and rotate certs monthly.

Action items I propose: 
1) EdgeFuse: confirm ECMP affinity option (hashing algorithm) and provide IP allowlist CSV.
2) Redwood (Karthik + Irene): update the diagrams to show dual-stream telemetry separation and add notes for mTLS CSR flow.
3) Schedule a 30-min ops handoff Wed 20 Jun 11:00 if the time works for EdgeFuse.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: EdgeFuse demarcation & uplink topology review (control-relay / data-striping)

Thanks everyone — great sync earlier today. Quick summary and next steps so procurement and engineering have a single reference: 

Summary decisions: 
- Demarc: BGP with ECMP chosen for production uplinks (EdgeFuse to provide hashing details).
- Control-plane: region-level relays with sticky-session hash; Redwood requires mTLS termination at relay only with region CSRs and monthly rotation.
- Telemetry: split streams. Non-audit traces over peering; audit logs over customer logging endpoint.

Action items (owners & due dates): 
- EdgeFuse (Maya): send IP allowlist + ECMP hashing config by Fri 23 Jun. (attachment: updated_allowlist.csv)
- Redwood (Karthik): publish diagram v1.1 with dual-telemetry streams and CSR process by Mon 26 Jun. (will attach redwood_controlplane_mapping_v1.1.xlsx)
- Procurement (Acme): confirm whether transit cross-connect cost will be capitalized or passed through. Please reply to this thread.

We will treat this as the canonical topology for the pilot. Once EdgeFuse provides the allowlist and hashing details we will move to checklist/acceptance.

Best —
